standard_prerequisites: the coherator DQ_X of lemma-better-coherator and its affine description RQ_X = DQ_X as the quasi-coherent sheaf attached to RGamma(X, K) (lemma-affine-coherator of the same chapter)
the induction principle for properties of quasi-compact quasi-separated algebraic spaces (lemma-induction-principle of the same chapter)

elementary distinguished squares (U subset W, f : V -> W) with quasi-compact quasi-separated W, quasi-compact open U and affine V, and the Mayer-Vietoris distinguished triangle of remark-explain-consequence
finite cohomological dimension on D_QCoh of the functors Rj_* for the thickenings j of the square (lemma-quasi-coherence-direct-image of the same chapter)
core_obligations: Prove that there exists an integer N = N(X) such that for K in D(O_X) with H^i(U, K) = 0 for all affine U etale over X and i outside [a, b], the cohomology sheaves H^i(DQ_X(K)) vanish for i outside [a, b + N]
proof_roadmap: Use the induction principle: the affine case holds with N = 0 because on affines DQ_X is given by the quasi-coherent sheaf associated to RGamma(X, K).

For an elementary distinguished square where the claim holds for U, V and U x_W V with bounds N(U), N(V), N(U x_W V), the restrictions K|_U, K|_V, K|_{U x_W V} satisfy the same vanishing, hence DQ applied to them vanishes outside [a, b + max of the three bounds].

The pushforwards Rj_* have finite cohomological dimension on D_QCoh, so a uniform N absorbs the shifts, and the distinguished triangle of the square gives the vanishing of H^i(DQ_X(K)) outside [a, b + N].
difficulty_reason: H3: an induction-on-spaces argument where the affine base case is trivial and the induction step combines three bounds through finite cohomological dimension of the pushforwards.
